'''SriLankan Airlines''' is the [[flag carrier]] of [[Sri Lanka]] and a member airline of the [[Oneworld]] [[airline alliance]]. It was launched in 1979 as '''Air Lanka''' following the termination of operations of the original Sri Lankan flag carrier, [[Air Ceylon]].{{cite news|url=http://www.ft.lk/2014/09/06/the-pioneering-air-ceylon-days/|title=The pioneering Air Ceylon days|work=Financial Times|access-date=23 December 2015|archive-date=24 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924042959/http://www.ft.lk/2014/09/06/the-pioneering-air-ceylon-days/|url-status=dead}} As of today, it is Sri Lanka’s largest airline by fleet size and number of destinations among local airlines. Its hub is [[Bandaranaike International Airport]]. Following its partial acquisition in 1998 by [[Emirates (airline)|Emirates]], it was re-branded and the current livery was introduced. In 2008, the government of Sri Lanka acquired all shares of the airline from Emirates.{{cite web|url=https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/emirates-walking-away-from-srilankan-220980/|title=Emirates walking away from SriLankan|first=Nicholas|last=Ionides|date=22 January 2008|website=Flightglobal.com|access-date=15 April 2019}} After ending the [[Emirates (airline)|Emirates]] partnership, it retained its re-branded name and logo.{{cite news|url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2010-06-07/news/28401427_1_dubai-s-emirates-airlines-pc-stake-cent-stake|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120616064216/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2010-06-07/news/28401427_1_dubai-s-emirates-airlines-pc-stake-cent-stake|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 June 2012|title=Sri Lankan Airlines buys back 43.6 pc stake from Emirates|newspaper=[[The Economic Times]]|access-date=24 April 2015}} SriLankan Airlines operates over 560 flights per week across Asia. SriLankan Airlines joined the [[Oneworld]] airline alliance on 1 May 2014.{{cite web|title = Our Airline|url = https://www.srilankan.com/corporate/en-US/Airline/profile|work=Srilankan|access-date=11 January 2016}} ==History== ===Management=== [[File:Lockheed L-1011-385-3 TriStar 500, AirLanka AN0846883.jpg|thumb|Air Lanka [[Lockheed L-1011 TriStar]] at [[Zurich Airport]] in 1998]] In 1979, after the removal of airline manager Nimesh Fernando, Sri Lanka's president, [[J. R. Jayewardene|JR Jayawardene]], initially did not interfere after entrusting the airline to Captain Rakitha Wickramanayake and the board of directors, consisting of industry officials and managers. The former prime minister of Singapore asked, "How could an airline pilot run an airline?" A 1986 presidential commission reported on the mismanagement of the board of the airline under President [[Dingiri Banda Wijetunga|Dingiri Wijetunga]]'s appointment of a retired general as chairman/MD with air vice marshals and a UNP attorney as executive directors. None of them knew how to run an airline.{{Cite web|date=2016-04-09|title=SriLankan Airlines: A Tale Of State Abuse & Mismanagement|url=https://www.colombotelegraph.com/index.php/srilankan-airlines-a-tale-of-state-abuse-mismanagement/|access-date=2021-12-28|website=Colombo Telegraph|language=en-US}} === Fleet expansion === Air Lanka was established as the flag carrier of Sri Lanka once the government shut down the bankrupt [[Air Ceylon]]. Air Lanka's initial fleet consisted of two [[Boeing 707]]s, leased from [[Singapore Airlines]]. One [[Boeing 737]] was leased from Maersk Air and maintained by Air Tara. On 24 April 1980, the lease ended; Air Lanka received a replacement [[Boeing 737]] leased from [[Royal Brunei Airlines]]. On 1 November 1980, Air Lanka commenced wide-body operations which were leased [[Lockheed L1011|Lockheed L1011-1 Tristar]] aircraft from [[Air Canada]]. On 15 April 1982, Air Lanka purchased a TriStar from [[All Nippon Airways]]. Another TriStar was leased from Air Canada whilst a third was purchased from All Nippon. With the introduction of TriStar aircraft, the Boeing 707s were phased out. On 1 May 1982, [[HAECO]] took over the maintenance of the two Air Lanka-owned TriStars, while Air Canada maintained the two leased TriStars. On 28 March 1980, Air Lanka signed a purchase agreement for two brand new [[Lockheed L1011-500|Lockheed L1011-500 TriStars]], the most advanced wide-body aircraft in the world at that time. The first L-1011-500 (4R-ULA, "''City Of Colombo''") was accepted on 26 August 1982, at [[Palmdale]], [[California]]. It was flown to [[Amsterdam]] as flight 566P. On 28 August, 4R-ULA left for its inaugural flight from Amsterdam to [[Colombo]] as UL566. It reached Colombo on 29 August. This was followed by the second Lockheed L1011-500, 4R-ULB, "''City of Jayewardenepura''". On 8 June 1984, the airline received its first [[Boeing 747-200B]] "''King Vijaya''" and the second joined later. The aircraft were used on flights to Europe and a few flights to southeast Asia. However, they were quickly retired in 1987. In 1994, Air Lanka became the Asian launch customer of the [[Airbus A340-300]].{{cite web |author= |date=2024-09-01 |title="SriLankan Airlines Turns 45, Celebrating A Journey of Milestones" |url=https://www.srilankan.com/en_uk/corporate/news-details/564 |website="www.srilankan.com" |location= |publisher= |access-date=2026-07-19}} ===Rebranding=== [[File:4R-ADB_-_Airbus_A340-311_-_SriLankan_Airlines.jpg|thumb|[[Airbus A340-300]]]] Air Lanka, which was state-owned, was partially privatised in 1998, with investment by the [[Emirates Group]] which signed an agreement with the Sri Lankan government for a ten-year strategic partnership. This agreement included exclusive rights for all aircraft ground handling and airline catering at Colombo-Bandaranaike airport for ten years. Emirates bought a 40% stake worth US$70 million (which it later increased to 43.6%) in Air Lanka and sought to refurbish the airline's image and fleet.Emirates buys into Air Lanka ''[[Australian Aviation]]'' issue 140 June 1998 page 17 The government retained a majority stake in the airline but gave full control to Emirates for investment and management decisions. In 1998, Air Lanka re-branded to SriLankan Airlines."World Airline Directory." ''[[Flight International]]''. 14–20 March 1990 [http://www.flightglobal.com/pdfarchive/view/1990/1990%20-%200709.html?search="Airlift International" 57]. SriLankan acquired six [[Airbus A330-200]]s to complement its fleet of [[Airbus A340-300]] and [[Airbus A320-200]]s. The A330-200 joined the airline between October 1999 and July 2000. The company's fourth A340-300 arrived at Colombo painted in the airline's new corporate livery. SriLankan upgraded its existing A340 fleet into a two-class configuration (business and economy class) whilst overhauling the interior to reflect the new corporate image. The airline gradually increased its number of destinations with more additions for regional markets, notably India and the Middle East. Whilst continuing expansion in the region, SriLankan commenced flying to [[Jeddah]], its third destination in Saudi Arabia, after [[Riyadh]] and [[Dammam]], thus increasing the number of destinations in the Middle East to nine. [[Jeddah]] became the airline's 51st destination overall. In 2008, Emirates notified the Sri Lankan Government that it would not renew its management contract,{{cite news|url=http://www.flightglobal.com/articles/2008/01/22/220980/emirates-walking-away-from-srilankan.html|title=Emirates walking away from SriLankan|publisher=Reed Business Information |access-date=24 April 2015}} which then expired on 31 March 2008. It claimed that the Sri Lankan Government was seeking greater control over the day-to-day management of the airline.[http://www.oag.com/oag/website/com/en/Home/Travel+Magazine/Executive+Travel/News+Briefing/Air+France+offers+inflight+calls+for+the+upwardly+mobile+010108 Management contract terminated] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080128143940/http://www.oag.com/oag/website/com/en/Home/Travel%2BMagazine/Executive%2BTravel/News%2BBriefing/Air%2BFrance%2Boffers%2Binflight%2Bcalls%2Bfor%2Bthe%2Bupwardly%2Bmobile%2B010108 |date=28 January 2008 }} January 2008, OAG, News briefing Emirates sold its 43.63% stake in the airline back to the [[Government of Sri Lanka]] in a deal that was finalised in 2010, thus ending their partnership.[http://www.businessweek.com/news/2010-07-07/sri-lanka-buys-emirates-stake-in-srilankan-airlines.html Sri Lanka Buys Emirates’ Stake in SriLankan Airlines] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100710231520/http://www.businessweek.com/news/2010-07-07/sri-lanka-buys-emirates-stake-in-srilankan-airlines.html |date=10 July 2010 }} Anusha Ondaatjie and Asantha Sirimanne, [[BusinessWeek]], 7 July 2010. ===Modern era=== [[File:4R-ALQ SriLankan Airlines Airbus A330-343 departing via Runway18 to Colombo (CMB - VCBI) @ Frankfurt Rhein Main - International (FRA - EDDF).jpg|thumb|left|4R-ALQ SriLankan Airlines [[Airbus A330-343]] departing via Runway 18 at [[Frankfurt Airport]] in 2016]] In 2008, when Emirates pulled out, the accumulated profit of SriLankan was Rs. 9.288 billion in that financial year. From 2008 to 2015, when the government ran it, the loss for the seven years was Rs. 128.238 billion (US$875 million).{{cite web|url=http://www.thedailystar.net/business/sri-lankas-loss-making-carrier-seeks-foreign-partner-1202626|title=Sri Lanka's loss-making carrier seeks foreign partner|website=The Daily Star|date=April 2016|access-date=2016-04-01}}{{cite web|url=http://www.sundaytimes.lk/160327/columns/from-paradise-to-hell-the-inside-story-of-how-srilankan-airlines-was-skyjacked-and-plundered-187767.html|title=From paradise to hell: The inside story of how SriLankan Airlines was skyjacked and plundered {{!}} The Sunday Times Sri Lanka|website=sundaytimes.lk|access-date=2016-04-01}} Following the ownership transfer, SriLankan began promoting Colombo as a hub for flights to Asia.{{cite web|url=http://www.lankabusinessonline.com/news/consolidating-colombo,-sri-lanka-as-an-aviation-hub/633092278|title=Consolidating Colombo, Sri Lanka as an aviation hub|access-date=24 April 2015|archive-date=3 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150403045313/http://www.lankabusinessonline.com/news/consolidating-colombo,-sri-lanka-as-an-aviation-hub/633092278|url-status=dead}} The first destination of the expansion plan was [[Shanghai]]; the route was initiated on 1 July 2010.[http://www.lankabusinessonline.com/fullstory.php?nid=560830907 Sri Lankan Airlines to fly to Shanghai] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100513141210/http://www.lankabusinessonline.com/fullstory.php?nid=560830907 |date=13 May 2010 }}, LBO, 10 May 2010 The airline commenced flights to [[Guangzhou]] on 28 January 2011.[http://www.lbo.lk/fullstory.php?nid=1554476079 SriLankan Airlines expands fleet, plans new destinations] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101125073926/http://lbo.lk/fullstory.php?nid=1554476079 |date=25 November 2010 }} LBO, 20 July 2010 [[File:Tokyo_Narita_International_Airport_DSC09749_(32434354114).jpg|thumb|SriLankan Airlines [[Airbus A330-243]] in the [[Oneworld]] livery]] SriLankan joined the [[Oneworld]] alliance on 1 May 2014. During 2014, it started to renew and increase its fleet, with purchases of Airbus A330 and A350 models. Currently, SriLankan operates an all-Airbus fleet except for its discontinued Air-Taxi services.{{cite news|title=Weliamuna Report recommends criminal prosecution of SriLankan Chairman, CEO|url=https://www.news.lk/fetures/item/6957-weliamuna-report-recommends-criminal-prosecution-of-srilankan-chairman-ceo|access-date=14 April 2018|agency=Government of Sri Lanka|publisher=news.lk|date=4 April 2015}} SriLankan retired their last [[Airbus A340-300]] on 7 January 2016 with its last scheduled flight from [[Chennai]] to Colombo. The airline terminated three European routes – Frankfurt, Paris and Rome – by the end of 2016. On 2020, the Frankfurt and Paris routes were resumed.{{cite news|url=https://www.ch-aviation.com/portal/news/85624-srilankan-airlines-to-resume-frankfurt-and-paris-services|title=SriLankan Airlines to resume Frankfurt and Paris services|newspaper=ch-aviation|date=2020-01-27|access-date=26 July 2022}} [[File:SriLankan Airlines AirTaxi - panoramio (edited).jpg|thumb|A [[de Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter|DHC-6 Twin Otter floatplane]] used as part of SriLankan's Air-Taxi service|right]] The airline absorbed the operations of sister carrier [[Mihin Lanka]] in October 2016, in a bid to create a single stronger national airline for Sri Lanka. Accordingly, SriLankan took over two of Mihin Lanka's aircraft and absorbed its route network, adding ten new destinations to SriLankan's route network. In October 2017, SriLankan launched direct daily non-stop flights to [[Melbourne]], Australia, its first new long-haul route in over five years and the most ambitious expansion to date. The flights restore a regular direct air link between Australia and Sri Lanka after a hiatus of sixteen years.{{Cite web|url=http://www.thesundayleader.lk/archive/20020616/spotlight.htm|title=The Sunday Leader Online - Spotlight|website=thesundayleader.lk|access-date=2017-10-30|archive-date=14 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210814100822/http://www.thesundayleader.lk/archive/20020616/spotlight.htm|url-status=dead}} This route has proved particularly popular and has been responsible with increased numbers of Australian tourists holidaying in Sri Lanka.{{Cite web |title=Surge in Aussie visitors following launch of SriLankan Airlines direct flights Down Under |url=https://www.srilankan.com/en_uk/corporate/news-details/205 |access-date=2024-03-18 |website=www.srilankan.com}} During the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], SriLankan performed cargo and operating relief flights. The [[Airbus A340|Airbus A340-300]] was delivered in 1994. The airline was the first in Asia to use the A340. The [[Airbus A330|Airbus A330-200]] aircraft were delivered later.{{citation needed|date=March 2024}} In 2012, SriLankan Airlines aimed to boost its fleet to 35 aircraft over the next five years and had talks with both Airbus and Boeing regarding a deal.{{cite web|url=http://www.dailynews.lk/2012/05/02/bus01.asp|title=SriLankan and Mihin Lanka to acquire 9 more aircraft|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120525083324/http://www.dailynews.lk/2012/05/02/bus01.asp|archive-date=25 May 2012}} SriLankan's former CEO Kapila Chandrasena stated that the carrier wanted to add six of either [[Airbus A330|Airbus A330-300]] or [[Boeing 777]] aircraft to its fleet to replace its Airbus A340-300s, with deliveries beginning in 2013–2014.{{cite web|url=http://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/routes-srilankan-in-talks-to-add-six-777s-or-a330s-362829/ |title=ROUTES: SriLankan in talks to add six 777s or A330s |work=Flight International |date=3 October 2011 }} In April 2013, it was announced that SriLankan Airlines had won government approval to acquire four [[Airbus A350 XWB|Airbus A350-900]] and seven A330-300 aircraft, with deliveries of the A330-300 starting from October 2014.{{cite web|url=http://www.lankabusinessonline.com/news/SriLankan_Airlines_to_get_13_Airbus_aircraft_with_7_A350s_-_Corrected/1532896203|title=SriLankan Airlines to get 13 Airbus aircraft with 7 A350s|access-date=24 April 2015|archive-date=2 February 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202153508/http://www.lankabusinessonline.com/news/SriLankan_Airlines_to_get_13_Airbus_aircraft_with_7_A350s_-_Corrected/1532896203|url-status=dead}} Deliveries for the ordered A350-900s were set to commence in 2019. A further three Airbus A350-900s were to be leased, with deliveries of these aircraft estimated by 2017. SriLankan retired its last Airbus A340-300 on 7 January 2016.[http://ch-aviation.com/portal/news/42959-srilankan-airlines-ends-commercial-a340-operations ch-aviation.com - SriLankan Airlines ends commercial A340 operations] 8 January 2016 As of January 2016, construction of the airline's first Airbus A350-900 started.{{cite web|url=http://www.airsrilanka.org/showthread.php?t=313&p=12310&viewfull=1#post12310|title=Sri Lanka Aviation|website=airsrilanka.org|date=January 2016 }} On 23 February 2015, SriLankan Airlines finalised a deal with [[Air Lease Corporation]] and [[AerCap]] to acquire two [[Airbus A321neo]] aircraft, one from each leasing firm.{{Cite web|url=https://www.ch-aviation.com/portal/news/35442-srilankan-finalizes-a321neo-leases-with-aercap-alc|title=SriLankan finalizes A321neo leases with AerCap, ALC|website=ch-aviation}} On 10 May 2016, due to financial difficulties, the airline announced it would cancel its order of eight A350 aircraft. The original livery featured: * Fuselage: A "cheatline" design consisting of two parallel red stripes running along the window line against a white upper fuselage * Titles: The name "AIRLANKA" was printed in bold, above the cheatline towards the front of the aircraft. * Tail Fin: A solid red and sported the corporate logo, a stylised [[vimana]] locally known as ''Dandu Monara'' (Flying Peacock Aircraft) of King [[Ravana]] of ancient ''Lanka'', [[Ravana]],{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=GkJOCgAAQBAJ&q=airlanka+dandu+monara&pg=PT169 |title=The Rough Guide to Sri Lanka |date=2 November 2015 |publisher=Rough Guides |isbn=9780241251263 }} as per the famous ''[[Ramayana]]'' mythology. The five "tail feathers" represent the "[[Five Precepts]]" (Pancasila) of [[Buddhism]] and the three "crown feathers" represent the "[[Triple Gem]]" (Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha) of Buddhism. Red reflects the predominant colour in the [[Flag of Sri Lanka|Sri Lankan national flag]], which represents the majority race in the country, the [[Sinhalese people|Sinhalese]]. ===Present livery (1999–present)=== [[File:Airbus_330-343_‘4R-ALR’_SriLankan.jpg|thumb|SriLankan Airlines [[Airbus A330-300]] in present livery]] Following a 40% acquisition by [[Emirates (airline)|Emirates]] in 1998, the airline was rebranded as SriLankan Airlines in 1999. The new visual identity was unveiled in Colombo with the arrival of a new [[Airbus A340]]. * Fuselage: A clean, all-white "Eurowhite" fuselage, removing the traditional cheatlines. * Titles: The wordmark "SriLankan" is written in a stylized, cursive-inspired font in dark blue. * Tail Fin: The ''Dandu Monara'' logo was replaced by a modern, abstract "Flying Bird" emblem prominently displayed against a white background. In Business Class, SriLankan offers full flat-bed seats on all of its long haul fleet with Audio Video on Demand (AVOD) facilities. The fully flat bed seat offers a 19.5 inches wide seat that can be reclined into a 180-degree 79 inches long bed. Each seat has a 15-inch personal IFE system. SriLankan's newest fleet additions will feature [[Thales Group|Thales]] Avant IFE, which features modern entertainment features and extended business class seats. Its [[A330-300]] fleet presents an all-aisle access seating in a 1-2-1 arrangement on Business Class.{{Cite news|url=https://www.ausbt.com.au/srilankan-airlines-brings-new-business-class-to-melbourne|title=SriLankan Airlines brings new business class to Melbourne|work=Australian Business Traveller|access-date=2018-11-24}} On its A320 family fleet, Business class is configured in a 2-2 layout, offering extra reclining seats, each seat with a width of 19 inches and a pitch between 39 and 49 inches.{{Cite web|url=https://www.seatguru.com/airlines/SriLankan_Airlines/fleetinfo.php|title=SriLankan Airlines Planes, Fleet and Seat Maps|website=seatguru.com|access-date=2018-11-24}} SriLankan provides in-seat entertainment in Economy class on all its wide-bodied aircraft and the vast majority of narrow-body aircraft. Its hub is at [[Bandaranaike International Airport]] (BIA).{{cite web|title = Accreditation – SriLankan Catering|url = http://www.srilankancatering.com/index.php/accreditation|website = srilankancatering.com|access-date = 2016-01-01|archive-date = 23 January 2016|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160123013146/http://www.srilankancatering.com/index.php/accreditation|url-status = dead}} SriLankan Catering's main line of business is in-flight catering to airlines that operate to [[Bandaranaike International Airport]].{{cite web|title = F&B Services for Aircraft Catering – SriLankan Catering|url = http://www.srilankancatering.com/index.php/our-services/f-and-b-services-for-aircraft-catering|website = srilankancatering.com|access-date = 2016-01-01|archive-date = 22 January 2016|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160122024801/http://www.srilankancatering.com/index.php/our-services/f-and-b-services-for-aircraft-catering|url-status = dead}} Its state-of-the-art flight kitchen at [[Bandaranaike International Airport|BIA]] has a capacity of 25,000 meals per day.{{cite web|title = Customer Service – SriLankan Catering|url = http://www.srilankancatering.com/index.php/our-environment/customer-service|website = srilankancatering.com|access-date = 2016-01-01|archive-date = 23 January 2016|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160123013222/http://www.srilankancatering.com/index.php/our-environment/customer-service|url-status = dead}} Incorporated in 1979, as Air Lanka Catering Services Limited with BOI status, SriLankan Catering commenced business as a joint venture with Thai Airways International. In 1998, when the joint venture agreement with Thai Airways International lapsed, Air Lanka Limited bought the shares of the joint venture partner and thus Air Lanka Catering Services became the fully owned subsidiary of SriLankan Airlines Limited. Thereafter the Company changed its name to SriLankan Catering (Private) Limited in September 2000.{{cite web|title = History – SriLankan Catering|url = http://www.srilankancatering.com/index.php/about-us/history|website = srilankancatering.com|access-date = 2016-01-01|archive-date = 23 January 2016|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160123040642/http://www.srilankancatering.com/index.php/about-us/history|url-status = dead}} ===Frequent flyer programme=== SriLankan's first [[frequent-flyer programme]] was called ''Serendib Miles'' and was abandoned in early 2000. It then became a partner of Emirates' [[Skywards]] frequent-flyer program. However, this agreement ceased to exist when the partnership between the two airlines concluded on 31 March 2008.[http://www.businesstraveller.com/news/sri-lankan-airlines-launches-ffp?LS=EMS169940 SriLankan Airlines launches FFP] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110708110219/http://www.businesstraveller.com/news/sri-lankan-airlines-launches-ffp?LS=EMS169940 |date=8 July 2011 }} Business Traveller, 26 March 2008. SriLankan subsequently launched ''FlySmiLes'', which has since added a variety of new reward partners to its program.[http://sundaytimes.lk/090125/Magazine/sundaytimestvtimes_08.html ‘FlySmiles’ announces exciting rewards] Sunday Times, 25 January 2009.{{cite web|url=http://www.flysmiles.com/ |title=FlySmiles | publisher=SriLankan Airlines | access-date=1 January 2016 }} New membership tiers were added after the airline's enrollment to the [[Oneworld|'''one'''world]] alliance to accommodate Oneworld membership tiers, gaining better privileges for members when aboard all Oneworld airlines. There are a total of four membership tiers {{as of|May 2014|lc=y}}. They are: *FlySmiLes Blue: Base tier *FlySmiLes Classic: Oneworld Ruby *FlySmiLes Gold: Oneworld Sapphire *FlySmiLes Platinum: Oneworld Emerald FlySmiles partners include all Oneworld airlines, [[Cinnamon Air]] and [[Etihad Airways]] and non-airlines partners like [[Abans]] and Spa Ceylon. ==Accidents and incidents== There are no hull losses reported till now, but six aircraft have been destroyed, and all of them have been a result of the civil conflict in Sri Lanka.{{citation needed|date=June 2025}} ===1980s=== {{Main|Air Lanka Flight UL512}} On 3 May 1986, a bomb planted by the terrorist group [[Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam|LTTE]] exploded on board Flight UL512 before [[takeoff]] at [[Bandaranaike International Airport]]. The bomb, which had been timed to explode in-flight, went off while the [[Lockheed L-1011|Lockheed L-1011 TriStar]] aircraft was on the ground, killing 21 of 128 passengers. Officials believe the bomb may have been concealed in crates of meat and vegetables that were being freighted to the [[Maldives]]. Other reports believe that the bomb was hidden in the aircraft's 'Fly Away Kit'. ===1990s=== In 1992, the right landing gear of an Air Lanka [[Boeing 737-200]] (registration 4R-ULL) at Madras Airport (now [[Chennai International Airport]]) failed upon landing and the right engine came into contact with the runway. The aircraft pulled to the right and finally came to a stop, with the nose wheel and right wing on the grass to the right of the landing runway. The right engine caught fire – extinguished by the airport safety services – and the 104 passengers and 12 crew evacuated the aircraft via the chutes on the left side without injury. The damage to the aircraft was substantial; the plane was subsequently repaired and sold.{{cn|date=November 2025}} The Indian Directorate General of Civil Aviation concluded that "the accident occurred as a result of a failure of the right-hand main landing gear beam during the landing due to pre-existing stress corrosion cracks and pits at its inboard lug hole and higher than normal landing loads contributed to its failure".[http://dgca.nic.in/accident/acc92.pdf] Civil Aviation Aircraft Accident Summary for the Year 1992 (DGCA, India) ===2000s=== {{Main|Bandaranaike Airport attack}} On 24 July 2001, a pre-dawn [[LTTE]] raid on the [[Sri Lanka Air Force]] hangar along [[Bandaranaike International Airport]] left at least 19 people dead, including all 14 [[LTTE]] cadres, two army commandos and three air force personnel. Two of SriLankan Airlines' [[Airbus A330]] planes (4R-ALE and 4R-ALF), one [[Airbus A320 family|A320]] (4R-ABA) and one of their [[Airbus A340|A340]] planes (4R-ADD) were destroyed. Two other aircraft were damaged (A340 4R-ADC and A320 4R-ABB). A number of military aircraft were also damaged and destroyed.{{cite web| year = 2001| url = http://www.janes.com/security/international_security/news/jir/jir010903_1_n.shtml| title = Intelligence failures exposed by Tamil Tiger airport attack| publisher = Jane's Intelligence Review| access-date =9 April 2008 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080225162532/http://www.janes.com/security/international_security/news/jir/jir010903_1_n.shtml |archive-date = 25 February 2008}} [https://asn.flightsafety.org/asndb/323259 Alt URL]{{cite web|url=http://www.aviation-safety.net/database/operator/airline.php?var=6660 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050315043711/http://aviation-safety.net/database/operator/airline.php?var=6660 |url-status=dead |archive-date=15 March 2005 |title=SriLankan Airlines (Aviation Safety Network) |publisher=Aviation-safety.net |date=4 March 2012 }} ===2020s=== On 13 June 2022, A potential [[mid-air collision]] was narrowly avoided, involving SriLankan Airlines Flight UL 504 (London → Colombo) and a [[British Airways]] aircraft flying to Dubai over Turkish airspace. According to reports UL 504 had been instructed by Ankara ATC to climb from 33,000 ft to 35,000 ft. The SriLankan crew's onboard systems, however, indicated that a British Airways aircraft was already at 35,000 ft, just about 15 miles (or 24 km) behind them. Demonstrating situational awareness, the UL 504 pilots refused to climb, even though they were cleared twice by ATC. Moments later, ATC corrected themselves and instructed UL 504 to remain at 33,000 ft upon realising the conflict. SriLankan Airlines later praised the pilots for their vigilance, crediting both their training and the aircraft's advanced communication and surveillance systems with averting what could have been a catastrophic mid-air collision.{{cite news |url=https://www.dailymirror.lk/latest_news/UL-504-avoids-biggest-possible-mid-air-collision-with-British-Airways/342-239067 |title=UL 504 avoids biggest possible mid-air collision with British Airways |access-date=4 November 2025 |work=[[Daily Mirror (Sri Lanka)|Daily Mirror]] |date=15 June 2022}}{{cite news |title=A Sri Lanka pilot refused order to climb to 35,000 feet. Then this happened |work=[[Hindustan Times]] |access-date=4 November 2025 |date=15 June 2025 |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/a-sri-lanka-pilot-refused-order-to-climb-to-35-000-feet-then-this-happened-101655301286172.html}} == Financial fallout == {{Chart|definition=SriLankan Airline financial performance.chart|data=SriLankan Airline financial performance.tab|width=450px|thumb=yes}} In 1998, Emirates won a proposal to handle the nation's flag airline, Air Lanka. Following that, Emirates rebranded the aging carrier as SriLankan and modernised its fleet with contemporary Airbus A330 aircraft. Emirates obtained ten years of management rights as part of the equity purchase. It later sold its ownership in the carrier for US$53 million, resulting in a nearly US$20 million loss.{{Cite web|date=2019-03-20|title=Emirates Management Of SriLankan Airlines|url=https://www.colombotelegraph.com/index.php/emirates-management-of-srilankan-airlines/|access-date=2021-12-28|website=Colombo Telegraph|language=en-US}} Sri Lanka currently has no [[bankruptcy]] protection act, and the only option for a closedown would be a complete [[liquidation]]. If the Government liquidates the airline, it will be compelled to write off this debt to the state banks and the [[Ceylon Petroleum Corporation]] (CPC). This could raise significant concerns about the two-state banks' liquidity by foreign rating agencies and could seriously jeopardise the prospects of Sri Lanka's entire banking sector. The Government as the guarantor would also be called upon for immediate repayment of the international bond worth US$175 million.{{Cite web|title=Corporate Collapses and Insolvency Regimes -The Sri Lankan Experience|url=https://www.lawnet.gov.lk/corporate-collapses-and-insolvency-regimes-the-sri-lankan-experience/|access-date=2021-12-28|website=LawNet|language=en-US}} Should that occur, aircraft rent payments would no longer be made, the risk premium for airlines leasing aircraft in Sri Lanka would increase, making the country an unappealing base for a carrier. However, this would be good news for [[Airbus]], which currently faces a more than US$1 billion claim for the airline over the [[A330]] and [[A350]] transactions for 2013.{{Cite web|title=Sri Lanka to Probe $2.3 bn Airbus Deal – Ilankai Tamil Sangam|url=https://sangam.org/sri-lanka-probe-2-3-bn-airbus-deal/|access-date=2021-12-28|website=sangam.org}} In 2016 and 2017, SriLankan's losses were impacted by costs related to the cancellation of its [[Airbus A350]] lease agreements. If the majority of the fleet were all due for heavy maintenance in later years, this could imply a significant charge of LKR 3 billion per annum for the prior years if restated. Such a change would make a further dent in the profits recorded during the Emirates era, as the maintenance cost was legitimately understated.{{Cite news|date=2017-06-16|title=SriLankan Airline's annual loss widens as Airbus compensation bites|language=en|work=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/srilankan-airlines-results-idUSL3N1JD1W7|access-date=2021-12-28}} SriLankan subsidiary [[Mihin Lanka]] never recorded an annual profit since its inception in 2007 and had an accumulated loss of LKR17.27 billion in 2016. For the 6-month period there was a loss of LKR 181 million and the remainder of the financial year it was budgeted to lose a further LKR billion. A few months after Mihin Lanka shut down, losses exceed LKR 13 billion. Most of the company's assets were acquired by SriLankan Airline on 29 October 2016.{{Cite web|last=Sirimane|first=Shirajiv|title=Mihin Lanka to wind up this year|url=https://www.dailynews.lk/2016/07/22/business/88251|access-date=2021-12-28|website=Daily News|language=en}} In 2020, SriLankan Airlines lost a little over US$200 million. In this period airline debt obligations today exceeded US$900 million (LKR 372 billion). The bulk of these appear to be debts to state banks and the [[Ceylon Petroleum Corporation|CPC]], both wholly owned by the [[Government of Sri Lanka]]. The airline also has at least one, sovereign guaranteed, internationally issued bond worth US$175 million.{{Cite web |last1= |first1= |date=2021-12-19 |title=Pay in US $, CPC tells SriLankan |url=https://www.newsfirst.lk/2021/12/19/pay-in-us-cpc-tells-srilankan/ |access-date=2021-12-28 |website=Sri Lanka News |language=en}} According to the Finance Ministry data, SriLankan lost LKR 24.5 billion from April to July 2021, as the company, which was already losing money, encountered further difficulties during the [[COVID-19 pandemic|SARS-CoV 2 outbreak]]. In the fiscal year ending March 2021, SriLankan lost LKR 58 billion.{{Cite web|date=2021-11-29|title=SriLanka Airlines loses Rs24.8bn from April to July 2021|url=https://economynext.com/srilanka-airlines-loses-rs24-8bn-from-april-to-july-2021-88319|access-date=2021-12-28|website=EconomyNext|language=en}} == Controversies == In March 2015, a report was released following a Board of Inquiry investigation into corruption at SriLankan during the time it was under the chairmanship of Nishantha Wickramasinghe. The board has reported that corruption was widespread and confirmed the allegations of Wickramasinghe's affairs.{{cite web |url=http://asianmirror.lk/news/item/8076-full-report |title=Shocking Revelations of Weliamuna Committee on SriLankan Airlines |work=Asian Mirror |date=7 April 2015 |access-date=9 April 2015 |archive-date=10 April 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150410191639/http://www.asianmirror.lk/news/item/8076-full-report |url-status=dead }} However, the Mahinda Rajapaksa Information Centre denied the allegations and accused the report of being biased and invalid, accusing the head of the committee of publicly supporting the current government in the elections and lacking technical knowledge about the aviation industry. It further claimed that he had been bribed to submit such a report as a publicity stunt to humiliate the previous government and that most of the points within it were untrue.{{cite web |url=https://www.mahinda.info/2015/04/blog-post_10.html |title=Truth about Weliamuna's allegations about air hostess incident (Sinhala) |publisher=Mahinda Rajapaksa Information Centre |date=10 April 2015 |access-date=10 April 2015 |archive-date=15 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210915131508/https://www.mahinda.info/2015/04/blog-post_10.html |url-status=dead }} The airline's short-lived Air-Taxi service and its mismanagement was found to have caused the loss of millions of dollars to the airline. In October 2015, the Presidential Commission of Inquiry to Investigate and Inquire into Serious Acts of Fraud, Corruption and Abuse of Power, State Resources and Privileges (PRECIFAC) attempted to summon Wickramasinghe to inquire about various irregularities in the airline; however, they were unable to locate him, and his wife claimed he had not come home for three years and that she was unaware of his whereabouts. Later, he notified PRECIFAC that he was abroad and was unable to give a statement.{{cite web|title = PRECIFAC unable to locate Nishantha Wickramasinghe|url = http://www.dailymirror.lk/92991/precifac-unable-to-locate-nishantha-wickramasinghe|website = dailymirror.lk|access-date = 2015-10-29}}{{cite web|title = Nishantha informs PRECIFAC he is abroad|url = http://www.dailymirror.lk/93103/precifac-he-is-aboard|website = dailymirror.lk|access-date = 2015-10-29}} == Potential privatisation == Following the economic crisis of 2022, the Sri Lankan government has been exploring approaches to [[Privatization|privatising]] several state-owned companies including SriLankan Airlines. In 2023, the Sri Lankan government set up the 'State-Owned Enterprise Restructuring Unit' (SRU) under the Ministry of Finance to assist in the privatisation of state-owned companies such as SriLankan Airlines.{{Cite web |title=Govt sets up restructuring Unit to assist in privatizing seven entitles including SriLankan, Litro - Breaking News {{!}} Daily Mirror |url=https://www.dailymirror.lk/breaking_news/Govt-sets-up-restructuring-Unit-to-assist-in-privatizing-seven-entitles-including-SriLankan-Litro/108-256428 |access-date=2023-03-23 |website=www.dailymirror.lk |language=English}} The [[National People's Power|NPP]]-led current government abandoned the plans for privatisation in September 2024.{{Cite web |title=NPP Govt. abandons plan to privatize SriLankan Airlines - Breaking News {{!}} Daily Mirror |url=https://www.dailymirror.lk/breaking-news/NPP-Govt-abandons-plan-to-privatize-SriLankan-Airlines/108-292708 |access-date=2024-10-14 |website=www.dailymirror.lk |language=English}} ==See also== * [[Colombo Marathon]], SriLankan Airlines is a sponsor of this primary marathon of Sri Lanka * [[Mihin Lanka]], a former government-owned low-fare leisure airline ==References== {{reflist}} * Birch, Doug. SriLankan Airlines is the flag carrier of Sri Lanka and a member airline of the Oneworld airline alliance. It was launched in 1979 as Air Lanka following the termination of operations of the original Sri Lankan flag carrier, Air Ceylon. As of today, it is Sri Lanka’s largest airline by fleet size and number of destinations among local airlines. Its hub is Bandaranaike International Airport.
Following its partial acquisition in 1998 by Emirates, it was re-branded and the current livery was introduced. In 2008, the government of Sri Lanka acquired all shares of the airline from Emirates. After ending the Emirates partnership, it retained its re-branded name and logo. SriLankan Airlines operates over 560 flights per week across Asia.
SriLankan Airlines joined the Oneworld airline alliance on 1 May 2014.
